coverage.non_warrant_content: The direction to work on folder records and handoff histories identifies the objects of examination. The hidden-trace possibilities, diagnostic interpretation, causal limitation, linkage assumption and prerequisite, and readiness requirements are captured in the claims.

Routine execution and bookkeeping include contacting the relevant reviewer, recording selection probabilities and unavailable histories, and daily reconciliation of arrivals, completions, returns, remaining queues, and actual volunteer hours. The reviewer step also locates the flag-generation rule. These instructions do not separately assert diagnostic success or sample adequacy. The proposed method, sampling and effort bounds, estimation exclusion, inconclusive classification, measurement prerequisite, and evidence-preservation distinctions are captured.

Routine observation and recording include noting each flag's location, supporting trace, age, and disposition, and observing daily queue changes and rework. The candidate signal types retain their explicit qualification as proposals rather than observations. The disposition distinction, staffed-hour comparison basis, and intervention distinction are captured.

Reassessment after one week is a routine review schedule without a separately stated outcome claim. The two-week assignment horizon and week-two evidence deadline are retained in the applicable claims. P024 also provides exhibition-inclusion context for C059. The local conclusion, causal limit, assignment rationales and constraints, estimation requirements, conditional scope decisions, and readiness counting rule are captured.

The preservation, effort-cap, and referral imperatives implement stated evidential, resource, and authority limits. Their material bounds and rationales are captured; routine execution details do not add separate outcome assertions. Alternative flag explanations, concealed-trace mechanisms, negative-result limits, sampling and aggregation limits, capacity distinctions, projection conditions, excluded conclusions, and intervention costs are all represented.
